blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:65:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:66:\section{Combined point measurements}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:67:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:68:The measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:69:$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}$ commute only approximately. The first goal of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:70:this chapter is to construct a single projective measurement that
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:71:simultaneously measures both, first at points and then along lines. The
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:72:source construction of the combined point measurement proceeds in three steps: the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:73:binary refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:74:$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:75:resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:76:pair $(r,s)$, and the following result of Natarajan and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:77:Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:78:linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:79:obtained by Fourier averaging. The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} below
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:80:instead forms the sandwich with field-valued outcomes and applies
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81:orthonormalization directly, without extending the local spaces.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:83:% Statement as in Theorem 10 of the cited source \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:84:% (arXiv:1610.03574): hypothesis as in its display (7), conclusion as in its
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:85:% display (8) with the normalization of the distance bound corrected, see
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:86:% rem:linearity-distance-normalization. The cited theorem imposes no upper bound
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:87:% on delta, asserts the exact linearity for all pairs (u, u'), and guarantees
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:88:% the closeness of L^u to O^u on average over uniformly random u only, in mean
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:89:% squared state-dependent distance; it is stated for an arbitrary density
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:90:% operator rho on a single Hilbert space, with the index group written {0,1}^n
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:91:% under bitwise XOR (here F_2^t, additively) and Obs(H) denoting the Hermitian
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:92:% unitaries, i.e. the binary observables of def:povm-conventions. In the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:93:% closeness conclusion an operator on H is compared with an operator on the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:94:% extension via its ampliation S ot Id. The cited theorem prints the closeness
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:95:% bound as delta for the squared operator distance; what its argument
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:96:% establishes is delta for the squared binary-measurement distance, i.e.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:97:% 2 delta for the squared operator distance, and the printed operator bound is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98:% false (docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex). The
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:99:% statement below carries the corrected operator bound together with the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:100:% equivalent measurement form. The mirror's quotation
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:101:% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:102:% inserts the restriction 0 <= delta <= 1, places the closeness conclusion,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:103:% together with the exact linearity, under the quantifier "for all u, u' in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104:% F_2^t", and appends "L^u = Id when u = 0"; none of these is part of the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:105:% cited theorem, and none is reproduced here. See rem:linearity-import.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:106:\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:107:	\label{thm:linearity}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:108:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable, MIPStarRE.QPBT.stateDepDistSq}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:109:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:110:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:111:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:112:	\uses{def:povm-conventions, lem:binary-measurement-distance}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:113:	Let $t$ be a positive integer and $\delta \ge 0$. Let $\rho$ be a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:114:	density operator on a Hilbert space $\hilb$ and let
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:115:	$\{\mathcal{O}^u\}$ be a set of binary observables indexed by
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:116:	$u \in \F_2^t$ acting on $\hilb$, such that on average over $u, u'$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:117:	chosen uniformly at random from $\F_2^t$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:118:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:119:		\E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'} \,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:120:		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \, \rho\big) \ge 1 - \delta\,.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:121:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:122:	Then there exist a Hilbert space $\hilb'$, a pure state
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:123:	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} \in \hilb'$, and binary observables
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:124:	$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ indexed by $u \in \F_2^t$ acting on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:125:	$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that, writing
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:126:	$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, the exact
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:127:	linearity
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:128:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:129:		\mathcal{L}^u \, \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:130:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:131:	holds for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$, and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:132:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:133:		\E_{u} \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:134:		\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le 2\delta\,,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:135:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:136:	where the expectation is over $u$ chosen uniformly at random from
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:137:	$\F_2^t$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:138:	$d_{\sigma}(S,T)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:139:	= \big(\Tr\big((S-T)^\dagger (S-T)\, \sigma\big)\big)^{1/2}$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:140:	denotes the state-dependent distance with respect to a density
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:141:	operator $\sigma$. Equivalently, in the distance $d^{\mathrm{bin}}_\sigma$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:142:	between the binary projective measurements associated with the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:143:	observables (Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}),
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:144:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:145:		\E_{u} \, d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:146:		\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \delta\,.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:147:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:148:	The cited source prints the first bound with $\delta$ in place of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:149:	$2\delta$; that normalization is false, and the bounds stated here are
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:150:	the ones its argument establishes
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:151:	(Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}).
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:152:\end{theorem}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:153:\begin{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:154:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:155:	\uses{lem:binary-measurement-distance, lem:blr-defect-identity,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:156:		lem:boolean-representation-stability}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:157:	This is Theorem~10 of Natarajan and Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity},
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:158:	whose Fourier--Naimark argument is followed; \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} invokes
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:159:	the result without proof. Write $\chi_v(u) = (-1)^{v \cdot u}$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:160:	$\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v = \E_u \, \chi_v(u) \, \mathcal{O}^u$ as in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:161:	Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:162:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:163:	\emph{From the correlation to the multiplicative defect.} For
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:164:	$u, u' \in \F_2^t$, expanding
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:165:	$(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'} - \mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^\dagger
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:166:	(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'} - \mathcal{O}^{u+u'})$ with
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:167:	$(\mathcal{O}^w)^2 = \Id$ and $\Tr \rho = 1$, as in the proof of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:168:	Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}, gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:169:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:170:		d_\rho\big(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}, \mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\big)^2
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:171:		= 2 - 2 \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^{u'} \mathcal{O}^u
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:172:		\mathcal{O}^{u'+u} \rho\big)\,,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:173:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:174:	the two cross terms being adjoint to each other. Exchanging the two
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:175:	coordinates of the uniform pair $(u,u')$, the hypothesis yields
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:176:	$\E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:177:	\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$. No commutation among the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:178:	observables is used.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:179:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:180:	\emph{The Fourier-square measurement and its Naimark rounding.} By
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:181:	Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} the operators
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:182:	$B^v = (\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^2$ are positive semidefinite and sum to
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:183:	$\Id$, so they form a POVM indexed by $\F_2^t$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:184:	Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper}, applied with an ancillary space $\hilb'$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:185:	of dimension $2^t + 1$ and with $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ the basis vector of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:186:	its extra direction, produces orthogonal projectors on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:187:	compressing along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ to the $B^v$; the residual
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:188:	projector of the construction is folded into the outcome $v = 0$, which
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:189:	gives a projective measurement $\{C^v\}$ resolving the identity on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:190:	$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ whose compression is still $\{B^v\}$, because the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:191:	$B^v$ themselves sum to $\Id$. Set
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:192:	$\mathcal{L}^u = \sum_v \chi_v(u) \, C^v$. Each $\mathcal{L}^u$ is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:193:	Hermitian, and the orthogonality of the $C^v$ together with
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:194:	$\chi_v(u) \chi_v(u') = \chi_v(u+u')$ gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:195:	$\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}$ for all $u, u'$;
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:196:	in particular $(\mathcal{L}^u)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_v C^v = \Id$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:197:	so the $\mathcal{L}^u$ are binary observables.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:198:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:199:	\emph{The distance/defect identity.} Since $\mathcal{L}^u$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:200:	$\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id$ are binary observables and $\rho'$ is a density
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:201:	operator, Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:202:	$d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:203:	= 2 - 2 \Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:204:	Compressing along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:205:	$\Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:206:	= \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \sum_v \chi_v(u) B^v \rho)$; averaging over $u$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:207:	turns $\E_u \chi_v(u) \mathcal{O}^u$ into $\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v$, and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:208:	expanding the three Fourier coefficients and summing the characters
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:209:	(Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}) gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:210:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:211:		\E_u \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho'\big)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:212:		= \sum_v \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^3 \rho\big)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:213:		= \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:214:		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho\big)\,.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:215:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:216:	Hence
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:217:	$\E_u d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:218:	= 2 - 2 \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:219:	\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:220:	= \E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:221:	\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$ by the first step. The measurement
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:222:	form follows by halving, through the normalization identity of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:223:	Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:224:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:225:	The obligations attached to the theorem at its point of use --- the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:226:	correspondence between the correlation hypothesis above and the relation
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:227:	$\approx_\delta$ of Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}, the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:228:	instantiation of $\rho$ as a reduced state of $\ket{\hat\psi}$, the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:229:	absorption of the ancilla register into padding of the strategy state,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:230:	and the identity $\mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$ --- are enumerated in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:231:	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import}. The proof of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:232:	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} below does not use this theorem.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:233:\end{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:234:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:235:\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:236:	\label{rem:linearity-import}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:237:	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form established by the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:238:	argument of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, with the normalization of its
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:239:	distance bound corrected as described in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:240:	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. Three features are
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:241:	load-bearing for the source's linearity-based proof of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:242:	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:243:	preserved without polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:244:	$2\delta$ in the conclusion for the squared operator distance, and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:245:	$\delta$ for the squared measurement distance, a constant factor absorbed
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:246:	by the relation $\approx_\delta$); the linearity of the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:247:	$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:248:	on average; and the hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:249:	theorem may be applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:250:	error the conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:251:	which no a priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:252:	$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:253:	only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:254:	that source argument only through averages over $u$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:255:	The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:256:	cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:257:	$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:258:	just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:259:	exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:260:	a strengthening of the theorem proved in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:261:	\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:262:	$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:263:	reproduced here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:264:	is not used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:265:	conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:266:	$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:267:	the identity. The factor of two of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:268:	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization} is not one of these
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:269:	differences. It is a defect of the cited statement itself: the mean
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:270:	squared operator bound printed in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:271:	\cite[Theorem~10]{Natarajan2017Linearity} is $\delta$, whereas the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:272:	calculation behind \cite[equation~(3)]{Natarajan2017Linearity} bounds
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:273:	the mean squared distance between the associated binary projective
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:274:	measurements, which is half the squared operator distance; the

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:305:\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:306:	\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:307:	As printed in \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, the conclusion of the quantum
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:308:	linearity theorem bounds the mean squared state-dependent operator distance
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:309:	$\E_u \, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id_{\hilb'})^2$ by
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:310:	$\delta$. That exact constant is the one printed in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:311:	\cite[Theorem~10]{Natarajan2017Linearity}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:312:	(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1079--1085}), once the distance
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:313:	there is read as the state-dependent operator distance. The quotation in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:314:	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar} does not assert it: there the conclusion reads
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:315:	$\mathcal{L}^u \approx_\delta \mathcal{O}^u$, and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:316:	Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} bounds the associated expectation only
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:317:	by $O(\delta)$, so that quotation absorbs a constant factor rather than
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:318:	claiming an exact one. The calculation behind the printed bound in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:319:	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the squared distance
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:320:	between the binary projective measurements associated with the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:321:	observables, which is half the squared operator distance, and then
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:322:	identifies the two quantities; the identification loses that factor. What
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:323:	the Fourier argument proves is the bound $\delta$ for the mean squared
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:324:	measurement distance, equivalently $2\delta$ for the mean squared operator
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:325:	distance, and the printed operator bound $\delta$ is refuted by a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:326:	four-point counterexample
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:327:	\cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization}. The normalization
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:328:	identities are recorded in Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance},
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:329:	and Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated and proved with the corrected
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:330:	bounds: $2\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator distance
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:331:	and $\delta$ for the mean squared measurement distance. The same
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:332:	conclusion, carrying the mean multiplicative defect as its hypothesis
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:333:	parameter, is recorded as
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:334:	Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-representation-stability}, from which the theorem
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:335:	is obtained by the substitution $\eta = 2\delta$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:336:\end{remark}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:755:	This is the mathematical content of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}: the

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:766:	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} from it.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:769:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:770:	\uses{lem:binary-measurement-distance, lem:blr-defect-identity,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:771:		lem:fourier-square-measurement, lem:naimark-rounding}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:772:	Let $\hilb'$ have orthonormal basis indexed by $\F_2^t$ together with one
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:773:	extra element $\bot$, and take $\ket{\mathrm{anc}} = \ket{\bot}$, the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:774:	initial state of the auxiliary register in the one-measurement Naimark
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:775:	construction of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper}. Apply that construction to
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:776:	the Fourier-square POVM $\{B^u\}$ of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:777:	Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement}. It returns
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:778:	projectors indexed by $\F_2^t \cup \{\bot\}$; the residual projector at
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:779:	$\bot$ is folded into the outcome $u = 0$, so that the resulting family
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:780:	$\{C^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ is still a family of orthogonal projectors summing
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:781:	to $\Id_{\hilb \ot \hilb'}$ and still compresses to $B^u$ along
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:782:	$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$, the latter because $\sum_u B^u = \Id_{\hilb}$. Set
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:783:	$\mathcal{L}^a = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, C^u$; orthogonality of the $C^u$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:784:	multiplicativity of the characters give
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:785:	$\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b = \mathcal{L}^{a+b}$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:786:	$(\mathcal{L}^a)^2 = \Id$, and each $\mathcal{L}^a$ is Hermitian because
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:787:	the characters are real. Since $\rho'$ is a density operator and both
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:788:	$\mathcal{L}^a$ and $\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}$ are binary
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:789:	observables, Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} gives
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:790:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:791:		d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^a, \mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:792:		= 2 - 2 \, \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{L}^a \,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:793:		(\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}) \, \rho'\big) ,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:794:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:795:	and taking the adjoint of the triple product, absorbing
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:796:	$\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}$ into the weight and compressing
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:797:	$\mathcal{L}^a$ along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ rewrites the trace as
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:798:	$\Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^a \, (\sum_u \chi_u(a) B^u) \, \rho\big)$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:799:	Averaging over $a$ and applying the overlap and cubic identities of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:800:	Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement} turns the average into
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:801:	$2 - 2 \, C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$, which is the mean multiplicative defect by
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:802:	Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}. No commutation among the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803:	$\mathcal{O}^u$ is used. The hypothesis then bounds the average by $\eta$.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1222:		\qquad x \in \F_q^m,\ z \in \F_q^m,\ \alpha \in \F_q,\

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1227:	$u = (u_X, u_Z, u_\alpha, u_\beta)$ and slope
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1228:	$v = (v_X, v_Z, v_\alpha, v_\beta)$, and let $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ be
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1229:	lines in $\F_q^m$ such that for every point
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1230:	$(x, z, \alpha, \beta) \in \ell$ it holds that $x \in \ell_X$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1231:	$z \in \ell_Z$. Then for any two polynomials
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1232:	$f \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X)$ and $g \in \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the polynomial
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1233:	$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \deg_{md+1}(\ell)$ is defined by
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1234:	\begin{equation}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1237:		= (u_\alpha + t \cdot v_\alpha)\, f(u_X + t \cdot v_X)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1238:		+ (u_\beta + t \cdot v_\beta)\, g(u_Z + t \cdot v_Z)\,,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1239:		\qquad t \in \F_q\,.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1240:	\end{equation}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1441:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SubLineWitness, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_subLineWitness}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1445:	% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lem:qld-sublines). The
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1446:	% line-point distribution over F_q^{2m+2} is built from the index
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1447:	% function chi of def:ld-question-distribution at dimension 2m+2, which

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1450:	There exists a distribution $D$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1451:	over tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, where $\ell$ is a line in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1452:	$\F_q^{2m+2}$ and $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ are lines in $\F_q^m$, with the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1453:	following properties:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1454:	\begin{enumerate}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1455:		\item The marginal distribution over $\ell$ is the same as the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1456:		marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1457:		% The source phrases the next property as: the marginal over
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1458:		% (ell_X, ell_Z) is "a mixture of the product distributions
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1459:		% D_{ALine,i} x D_{ALine,j} and D_{DLine,i} x D_{DLine,j}". Those
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1460:		% products are distributions over pairs of line-point pairs, not
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1461:		% over pairs of lines, so the phrase does not define the asserted
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1462:		% marginal distribution on pairs of lines as written; the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1463:		% formulation below states the mixture at the level of the joint
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1464:		% law of (ell_X, ell_Z, u), which is what the proofs of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1465:		% lem:claim-17-2 and lem:claim-17-3 use.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1466:		\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1467:		lying on $\ell$, it holds that $u_X \in \ell_X$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1468:		$u_Z \in \ell_Z$. Moreover, the joint distribution of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1469:		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$, for $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z) \sim D$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1470:		$u$ chosen uniformly at random on $\ell$, is a mixture of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1471:		components indexed by a type
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1472:		$\mathrm{v} \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and indices
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1473:		$i, j \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ with the following two properties
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1474:		within the component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$: the pair
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1475:		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is distributed according to the product of the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1476:		marginal distributions on lines of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1477:		$D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1478:		point $u_X$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_X$ and likewise the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1479:		point $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_Z$. Equivalently,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1480:		since under each restricted distribution the point is uniformly
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1481:		distributed on the line conditionally on the line: within the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1482:		component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$, the pair
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1483:		$((\ell_X, u_X), (\ell_Z, z'))$, where $z'$ is a uniformly random
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1484:		point of $\ell_Z$ sampled independently of $u$, is distributed

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1486:		symmetrically the pair $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, u_Z))$, with $x'$

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1488:		$u$, is distributed according to
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1489:		$D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$. (No assertion is made
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1490:		about the joint conditional law of the pair $(u_X, u_Z)$.)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1491:		\item If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, then $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1492:		axis-parallel.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1493:	\end{enumerate}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2365:\begin{remark}[Divisibility obstruction in the application of the classical
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2366:	soundness theorem]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2367:	\label{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2368:	Definition~\ref{def:ld-game} defines the classical low individual
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2369:	degree game only when its dimension parameter divides $q$: the index
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2370:	function $\chi$ of the question distribution
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2371:	(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}) partitions $\F_q$ into
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2372:	classes of equal size, one for each coordinate. The same divisibility
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2373:	underlies the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2374:	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist} instantiated at dimension
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2375:	$2m+2$), and with it the statements of Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2376:	and~\ref{lem:qld-4-13} and the proofs of all three of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2377:	Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}, \ref{lem:qld-4-13}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2378:	and~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. The condition that $2m+2$ divide $q$ does not
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2379:	follow from admissibility of $(q,m,d)$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2380:	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), which supplies only that $m$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2381:	divides $q$; indeed the two are jointly satisfiable only in a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2382:	degenerate range. An admissible field size
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2383:	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) is a power of two, so $m$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2384:	dividing $q$ forces $m$ to be a power of two; for $m \ge 2$ the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2385:	integer $m+1$ is odd and exceeds $1$, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ divides no
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2386:	power of two, while for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2387:	every admissible $q$ except $q = 2$. The source proof in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2388:	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar} performs the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2389:	without addressing the divisibility. The statements above are
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2390:	therefore retained in their source form, and for admissible
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2391:	parameters with $m \ge 2$ their proofs, like the source's, are
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2392:	blocked at the marked steps, so the conclusions are not established
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2393:	for such parameters, here or in the source. A proof covering every
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2394:	admissible parameter tuple requires a formulation of the game, of its
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2395:	question distribution, and of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} that
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2396:	applies to dimensions not dividing $q$; the missing step and the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2397:	candidate repairs are analyzed in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2398:	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2399:\end{remark}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2402:% coordinate change for the LDT consistency conclusions and the compression of

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2404:\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the consistency conclusions in directly indexed coordinates]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2405:	\label{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2406:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2407:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2408:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2409:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2410:	\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, def:admissible-size,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2411:		lem:direct-ld-consistency-defect-equivalence}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2412:	This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records three
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2413:	consistency implications in the directly indexed coordinates, in which the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2414:	sampled coordinate is carried by the question itself rather than by a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2415:	residue class of $\F_q$; see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}. The
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2416:	hypothesis of each implication is an arbitrary consistency relation
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2417:	between measurement families of the stated kinds; no implication produces
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2418:	such a relation or constructs the measurements it relates. They may in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2419:	particular be applied to the three consistency relations in the conclusion
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2420:	of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2421:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2422:	Fix a directly indexed parameter tuple $D=(q,m,d,k)$, where $m,d,k \ge 1$
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2423:	are integers and $q$ is an admissible field size
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2424:	(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}). In contrast with the parameters of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2425:	the classical game (Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}), no divisibility
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2426:	condition $m \mid q$ is imposed; dropping that condition is the only
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2427:	difference between the two parameter domains. Let $\delta\in\R$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2428:	The following three implications hold:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2429:	\begin{enumerate}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2430:		\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be a projective strategy for the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2431:		      directly indexed game, fix
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2432:		      $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(k)=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and let
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2433:		      $G^{\mathrm B}$ be a projective measurement on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2434:		      $\hilb_{\mathrm B}$ indexed by single $m$-variate
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2435:		      polynomials of individual degree at most $d$, consistency with
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2436:		      error $\delta$ between the coordinate-$r$ LDT point family of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2437:		      Alice and the evaluation family of $G^{\mathrm B}$ implies
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2438:		      that the corresponding directly indexed point/polynomial
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2439:		      off-diagonal defect, evaluated on $\psi$ and averaged uniformly
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2440:		      over $u\in\F_q^m$, is at most $\delta$;
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2441:		\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be a projective strategy for the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2442:		      directly indexed game, fix
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2443:		      $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(k)=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and let
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2444:		      $G^{\mathrm A}$ be a projective measurement on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2445:		      $\hilb_{\mathrm A}$ indexed by the same single polynomials,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2446:		      consistency with error $\delta$ between its evaluation family
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2447:		      and the coordinate-$r$ LDT point family of Bob implies the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2448:		      corresponding directly indexed polynomial/point defect bound
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2449:		      $\delta$, again averaged uniformly over $u\in\F_q^m$;
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2450:		\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be an arbitrary strategy for the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2451:		      directly indexed game, with no projectivity assumption on $S$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2452:		      and let $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ be projective
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2453:		      measurements on the two players' spaces indexed by single
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2454:		      polynomials. Consistency with error $\delta$ between these two
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2455:		      constant LDT measurement families over the one-element question
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2456:		      set implies that the corresponding directly indexed
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2457:		      polynomial/polynomial defect is at most $\delta$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2458:	\end{enumerate}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2459:	Thus the first two implications concern one fixed coordinate and the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2460:	third concerns no coordinate. All three use single-polynomial projective
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2461:	measurements; they do not construct a joint measurement of a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2462:	$k$-tuple of polynomials.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2463:\end{lemma}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2464:\begin{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2465:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2466:	For each implication, the density-state consistency relation is changed
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2467:	to the identical off-diagonal defect on the vector $\psi$. The first two
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2468:	defects are then reindexed by the point and scalar bijections and by
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2469:	polynomial evaluation; the third is reindexed by the polynomial-outcome
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2470:	bijection. These changes preserve the bound $\delta$ exactly.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2471:\end{proof}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2473:\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the compression of a correlated residue register]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2474:	\label{lem:direct-ld-residue-compression}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2475:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_pointPolynomial_compression}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2476:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_polynomialPoint_compression}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2477:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2478:	\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:admissible-size}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2479:	This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records two
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2480:	compression identities between the classical low individual degree game
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2481:	and its directly indexed presentation.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2482:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2483:	Fix parameters $\mathsf{ldparams}=(q,m,d,k)$ of the classical game as in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2484:	Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}: integers $m,d,k \ge 1$, an admissible field
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2485:	size $q$ (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}), and $m \mid q$. Unlike
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2486:	in Lemma~\ref{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}, the divisibility
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2487:	belongs to the domain here, since it is what gives the residue register
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2488:	below its dimension; the directly indexed parameters appearing on the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2489:	other side of the identities are this tuple with the divisibility
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2490:	condition dropped. Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2491:	game, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to each
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2492:	player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the classes of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2493:	the index function $\chi$ of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2494:	Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}; the two copies of that
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2495:	register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2496:	polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm B}$ on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2497:	$\hilb_{\mathrm B}\ot\C^{q/m}$, let $\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ be the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2498:	normalized average of its diagonal blocks over the residue register.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2499:	Then, over a uniformly random point $u\in\F_q^m$, the off-diagonal
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2500:	defect between Alice's point measurement and the evaluation of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2501:	$G^{\mathrm B}$ on the extended strategy equals the defect between
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2502:	Alice's original point measurement and the evaluation of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2503:	$\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ on $(\psi,A,B)$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2504:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2505:	Similarly, for every polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm A}$ on
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2506:	$\hilb_{\mathrm A}\ot\C^{q/m}$, compression gives equality between
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2507:	the extended polynomial/point defect and the defect between the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2508:	evaluation of $\bar G^{\mathrm A}$ and Bob's original point
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2509:	measurement. No projectivity hypothesis is imposed on the strategy or
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2510:	on either polynomial-tuple POVM.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2511:\end{lemma}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2512:\begin{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2513:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2514:	The point measurement of the extended strategy is the block-diagonal
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2515:	amplification of the original point measurement, while polynomial
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2516:	evaluation commutes with averaging the diagonal blocks. The quadratic
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2517:	form of the correlated state against each mixed pair of operators is
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2518:	therefore the quadratic form of the original state against the
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2519:	compressed pair, and summing the off-diagonal terms gives both identities.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2520:\end{proof}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2522:\begin{remark}[Compression of two polynomial measurements]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2523:	The preceding lemma does not compare defects in which both families are

blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2664:The following three formalization-only auxiliary statements concern real
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2665:functions and numerical parameters, independently of the standing strategy
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2666:assumptions of this chapter. They isolate calculations supporting
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2667:Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}, \ref{lem:qld-4-13}, and \ref{lem:qld-4-7}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2668:in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}; they assert no measurement construction.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2669:Here $p(x)=\poly(x)$ means that $p:\R\to\R$ satisfies
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2670:$0\le p(x)\le A x^r$ for all $x\ge0$, for some $A\ge1$ and $r>0$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2671:Similarly, $f(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$ means
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2672:$0\le f(x,y)\le B(x^s+y^t)$ for all $x,y\ge0$, for some $B\ge1$ and
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2673:$s,t>0$. These are the corrected error conventions of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2674:\cite{gap:qpbt_polynomial-error-square-root,gap:qpbt_pasting-product-error}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2675:The functions are defined on all real arguments; these bounds concern their
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2676:nonnegative domains.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2677:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2678:\begin{theorem}[Polynomial error after conditioning]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2679:	\label{thm:qld-conditioned-polynomial-bound}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2680:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_conditioned_polynomial_bound}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2681:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2682:	Let $p(x)=\poly(x)$, let $f(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$, and fix $c\ge1$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2683:	There exists $g(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$ such that for every
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2684:	$\eps,\rho\ge0$ and every $\mu\in[1/2,1]$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2685:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2686:		\min\left\{1,\,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2687:			\mu f\left(\rho,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2688:				\frac{8p(\eps)+c(\eps+\sqrt{\eps})}{\mu}\right)+\rho
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2689:		\right\}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2690:		\le g(\eps,\rho).
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2691:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2692:	This scalar estimate supports the pasting substitution in the proof of
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2693:	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}. The interval for $\mu$ is an explicit
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2694:	hypothesis of this auxiliary estimate.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2695:\end{theorem}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2696:\begin{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2697:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2698:	Choose $A,r,B,s,t$ as in the polynomial bounds above, and set
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2699:	$\alpha=\min\{r,1/2\}$, $\beta=\min\{s,1\}$, and $L=8A+2c$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2700:	For $0\le\eps,\rho\le1$, the numerator in the argument of $f$ is at
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2701:	most $L\eps^\alpha$, and division by $\mu\ge1/2$ costs at most a
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2702:	factor of two. The polynomial bound on $f$, together with $\mu\le1$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2703:	therefore gives the required inequality with
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2704:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2705:		g(\eps,\rho)=\bigl(B(1+(2L)^t)+1\bigr)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2706:			\bigl(\eps^{\alpha t}+\rho^\beta\bigr).
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2707:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2708:	If either $\eps>1$ or $\rho>1$, this function is at least one, which
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2709:	bounds the minimum. All its exponents are positive.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2710:\end{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2711:
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2712:\begin{theorem}[Polynomial composition with the dimension factor]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2713:	\label{thm:qld-combining-polynomial-bound}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2714:	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combining_polynomial_bound}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2715:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2716:	Let $p(x)=\poly(x)$, let $f(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$, and fix $c\ge0$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2717:	There exists $g(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$ such that for all
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2718:	$\eps,\rho\ge0$ and all real $D\ge1$,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2719:	\[
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2720:		\min\left\{1,\,
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2721:			c\left(p(\eps)^{1/2}+\sqrt D
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2722:				\left(f(\eps,\rho)^{1/4}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2723:					+p(\eps)^{1/4}+\eps^{1/4}\right)\right)
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2724:		\right\}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2725:		\le D\,g(\eps,\rho).
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2726:	\]
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2727:	The factor $D$ is retained in this numerical consequence of the first
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2728:	route in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, as explained in
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2729:	Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-13-source-defects}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2730:\end{theorem}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2731:\begin{proof}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2732:	\leanok
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2733:	Choose $A,r,B,s,t$ as in the polynomial bounds and put
blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:2734:	$\alpha=\min\{r/4,s/4,1/4\}$ and
